methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional investment in deep AI fluency outside metro corridors, potentially enabling peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could distribute capability beyond traditional tech hubs if sustained and connected to workforce pipelines.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops targeting the 'technology gap' signal grassroots capability-building in a defense-oriented region, suggesting distributed access pathways that could deepen fluency if participants move beyond platform consumption to actual skill development.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA explicitly targets community impact and education beyond elite students, creating potential infrastructure for distributed deep learning if the initiative reaches beyond Richmond's urban core into surrounding underserved communities.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Mounting AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce reveals the competitive intensity concentrating in established metro centers, where employers demand immediate AI fluency that favors those with prior access to deep training over those relying on shallow platform adoption.

signals.title: Virginia's AI boom quietly drained the entire regional electricity grid - Yahoo Finance
signals.signal_reading: The complete drainage of regional electricity capacity by Virginia's AI data center boom demonstrates how infrastructure constraints paradoxically reinforce geographic concentration—only areas with massive grid investment can participate, deepening the NoVA-centric capability divide.
